title: Transform Self-Love into Empathy: The Law of Narcissism

chapterBreakdown.gentle: The chapter on narcissism stays useful because it names a pattern people often feel before they can explain it. This law treats narcissism as a spectrum, arguing that nearly everyone begins from self-absorption and that the real developmental move is not to abolish self-love but to convert some of its energy into empathy. This is why Greene describes a spectrum. Some people stay shallowly self-absorbed. Some become deeply manipulative and exploitative. Others develop enough security to look outward and read what other people are actually feeling. Healthy narcissism is not self-hatred. It is a stronger self that no longer needs to make every encounter mirror its needs. The practical discipline is empathy. Watch what other people fear, want, and defend. Listen past your urge to steer attention back to yourself. Use your own hunger for significance as evidence of the same hunger in everyone around you. Empathy widens perception without erasing boundaries. That softer honesty is already a practical advantage.
